'''Taruna Madan Gupta''' ({{langx|hi|तरुना मदान गुप्ता}}) (Taruna Gupta), born on 14 May 1968 in [[New Delhi]], is an Indian scientist F and Head of the Department of Innate Immunity<ref>{{cite web|title=Lab web page of Dr. Taruna M. Gupta|url=http://www.nirrh.res.in/staff/scientific/DrTaruna_resume.htm|access-date=23 August 2011|archive-date=13 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170613131505/http://www.nirrh.res.in/staff/scientific/DrTaruna_resume.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Dr. Taruna M. Gupta on ICMR web site|url=http://www.icmr.nic.in/icmrsql/biodata.asp?expno=00011815}}</ref> at the [[National Institute for Research in Reproductive Health]] (NIRRH) in [[Mumbai]], [[India]]. She has extensively worked on [[Aspergillosis]]<ref>{{cite news|title=Breakthrough in Allergy Treatment|url=https://www.thehindu.com/2004/01/11/stories/2004011102901000.htm | location=Chennai, India | date=11 January 2004 |work=[[The Hindu]]| accessdate=2 February 2019 }}{{dead link|date=September 2026|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> and Lung Surfactant Proteins (SP-A, SP-D), with her research now more focused on role of Innate Immunity in host-pathogen interactions.

==Education and personal life==
*[[Bachelor of Pharmacy]] (B.Pharm.) (year 1989, Gold Medallist) - Delhi Institute for Pharmaceutical Education and Research (DIPER), [[University of Delhi]]
*[[Master of Pharmacy]] (M.Pharm.) (year 1991, Gold Medallist) - Delhi Institute for Pharmaceutical Education and Research (DIPER), [[University of Delhi]]
*[[Ph.D.]] - Jointly with Delhi Institute for Pharmaceutical Education and Research (DIPER), [[University of Delhi]] and [[Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology]] (IGIB), [[New Delhi]].

Taruna is married to Dr. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta ''Ph.D''. who is an accomplished professional in the area of Medical Device and In Vitro Diagnostic Devices (IVD) and Founder of PUNJ (Psoriasis Undone for New Joy) in India.<ref>{{cite web|title=Biography of Dr. Sanjeev Kumar Gupta on Max Healthcare|url=https://www.maxhealthcare.in/doctor/dr-sanjeev-kumar-gupta}}</ref> They have one son, Urit Gupta.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hindustan Times|url=https://www.hindustantimes.com/mumbai/first-support-group-started-by-patients/story-cDi1rNj1J2YCls0i2FtRrN.html|date=26 April 2012}}</ref>

==Professional life==
* Post-doctoral research on "Role of lung collections in genetic predisposition to aspergillosis" as Senior Research Associate at [[Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology]] (IGIB) ([[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], CSIR), Delhi, India.
* Doctoral and post-doctoral research at [[Medical Research Council (UK)|Medical Research Council]] (MRC) Immunochemistry Unit, University of Oxford, Oxford, UK (July 1996 - September 1996 and July 2000 - September 2000).
* Scientist "C" <ref>{{cite web|title=Dr Taruna M. Gupta as scientist in IGIB, Delhi|url=http://www.csir.res.in/external/heads/aboutcsir/lab_phone/igib.htm}}</ref> in Allergy and Infectious Diseases Department, [[Institute of Genomics and Integrative Biology]] (IGIB) ([[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]], CSIR), Delhi, India (2002–2007)
*Scientist "F" at NIRRH since 2018

==Publications and patents==
Taruna M. Gupta is a contributing author on over 100 peer-reviewed journal articles, and has been cited over 3000 times.<ref>{{cite web|title=Publications of Dr. Taruna M. Gupta on Google Scholar|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=SO3HesYAAAAJ&hl=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Publications of Dr. Taruna M. Gupta on Pubmed|url=https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/?term=madan%20t}}</ref> Most of these articles concern the research of fungal [[aspergilosis]] and lung [[surfactant]] proteins.

She has three patents concerning the identification and treatment of aspergilli.<ref>{{cite web|title=Patents listing of IGIB|url=http://www.igib.res.in/pme/patents.htm}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Patents of Dr. Taruna M. Gupta|url=http://www.patentgenius.com/inventedby/MadanTarunaDelhiIN.html}}</ref>

==Awards and recognition==
* Received Indo-US Wistemm WIS Fellowship (IUSSTF) (2018). Under fellowship work was done at Brigham & Women's Hospital, Harvard Medical School, Boston, USA
*Young Women Bioscientist award from [[Indian Science Congress Association]] (2004).
* [[Council of Scientific and Industrial Research]] (CSIR) Young Scientist Award<ref>{{cite web|title=CSIR Young Scientist Award, Year 2003|url=http://www.csir.res.in/csir/external/heads/aboutcsir/annual_report/2003-2004/bio_science.htm}}</ref> (Category -Life Sciences) (Year 2003).
* [[Indian National Science Academy]] (INSA) Young Scientist Medal Award (Category -Medical Sciences) (Year 1998).

'''Product Development:''' Developed ELISA kits for detection of Aspergillosis in serum under DBT Task Force
